perf.summary: O(n^2) insertion sort over 8-byte Pair structs; each shift moves the whole 8-byte struct. Radix sort on the Key with a parallel value array, or sorting an index, gives O(n) and moves less data.
perf.currentCost: O(n^2) struct moves; each ptr[j+1]=ptr[j] copies 8 bytes (Key+Value). Doubles the memory traffic of a key-only sort and keeps the serial dependency chain.
perf.proposedChange: For non-tiny len, LSD radix sort by Key (4 passes) writing whole Pair entries into a scratch Pair buffer; sign-flip the top byte of Key for signed correctness. Alternatively radix-sort an int[] permutation of indices to avoid moving the 8-byte payload during intermediate passes, applying the permutation once at the end.
perf.rationale: O(4n) vs O(n^2). The index-permutation variant moves only 4-byte indices during the 4 passes and writes the final 8-byte payload exactly once, halving payload memory traffic versus shuffling Pairs every pass.
perf.risk: Signed Key ordering via top-byte XOR 0x80000000. Radix is not stable across the chosen byte order unless implemented LSD (it is) so equal Keys retain input order — actually LSD radix IS stable, which insertion sort also is on Key, so behavior is preserved for ties (good). Needs scratch buffer: additive overload, do not break unchecked Run.

perf.summary: Pair is implicitly auto-layout; add [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)] (and it is already naturally 8-byte aligned/blittable) to lock layout for interop and Burst SoA reasoning.
perf.currentCost: Default struct layout is sequential for blittable structs in practice, but unannotated layout can theoretically be reordered and is less self-documenting for a type passed via raw pointers.
perf.proposedChange: Annotate `[StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)] public struct Pair`. No size change (two ints = 8 bytes, no padding).
perf.rationale: Guarantees Key-then-Value byte order so callers can blit/upload buffers and so radix passes can index the Key field by known offset. Documents blittability for Burst.
perf.risk: None semantically; layout is already what callers expect. Purely a hardening/clarity change.
